title: AuditEvent
description: One record in the append-only audit log: a durable account of a consequential action the oversight dashboard orchestrated — an agent spawn, a human approval decision, or a branch merge. The cockpit is the SOLE writer (one append-only JSONL log via the existing atomic-write helper, ADR-0004 local-JSON, no DB); it records both the events it performs directly and the rails-mediated ones it drives via the control-plane CLI shell-out. v9 adds `controlState` — the runtime-governance record of WHICH guardrails were in force, whether the gate was blocking, and who decided — REQUIRED on 'approval' events (see the conditional below) so an approval can never be recorded without its control context. KNOWN LIMITATION: actions taken against the rails CLI directly (outside the dashboard) are not captured by this log yet — there is no second writer this phase. Permissive (additionalProperties:true) so emitters can attach event-specific detail under `payload` without a schema bump.

schemaVersion.description: The contracts surface version this record was written under (derived from the single-source schema-version.json sidecar), so a reader can interpret older records as the surface evolves.

ts.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when the event occurred (UTC, e.g. 2026-06-08T14:03:11.000Z).

eventType.description: The kind of consequential action recorded: 'spawn' (an agent session was started), 'approval' (a human decided on a gated/danger-zone request), or 'merge' (a branch was merged).

actor.description: Who or what initiated the action — a human operator identity for approvals, or an orchestrator/system identifier for automated steps. Null when not attributable.

subjectId.description: Identifier of the thing the event acted ON (e.g. the approval-request id for an approval, the branch ref for a merge). Null when not applicable.

sessionId.description: The agent session this event relates to, when one exists (e.g. the spawned session for a 'spawn' event). Null when no session is involved.

projectKey.description: The project this event belongs to, scoping the record to one workspace in a multi-project view. Null when not project-scoped.

decision.description: For an 'approval' event: the human decision recorded (e.g. approved / denied). Null for non-approval events.

outcome.description: The result of the action once known (e.g. succeeded / failed / skipped). Null while pending or not applicable.

source.description: Which control surface the event flowed through: 'cockpit' for an action the dashboard performed directly, 'harness' for a rails-mediated action the dashboard drove via the control-plane CLI shell-out.

correlationId.description: An id that ties related events together across surfaces (e.g. a request that triggers a spawn then an approval then a merge), so a multi-step flow can be reconstructed. Null when standalone.

controlState.description: The control state in force WHEN the event occurred — the runtime-governance record that makes the log auditable as enforcement, not just observation: which guardrails were active, whether the gate blocked execution, and who decided. Required (with gateType + decisionMaker) on 'approval' events via the conditional below; optional but encouraged elsewhere (e.g. a spawn records the policies the agent was launched under). Fields the emitter does not know are omitted or null — NEVER fabricated.

gateType.description: How the control point behaved: 'hard' (execution was blocked until the decision), 'soft' (advisory — execution could proceed), or 'policy' (the decision changed the control configuration itself, e.g. a trust grant). Null/omitted when the event is not a control point.

decisionMaker.description: Who made the decision this event records: 'human' (an operator acted through the dashboard) or 'auto' (an automated policy/orchestrator step). Null/omitted when no decision was involved.

policiesInForce.description: The guardrails active at event time, as short stable identifiers (e.g. 'budget-cap:12', 'adversarial-verify:1x1', 'quarantine:read-only', 'worktree-isolation', 'trust-store:default-deny'). List only what was ACTUALLY in force — an empty list means 'none known', not 'none'.

permissionMode.description: The session permission mode in force, when known (e.g. a guarded default vs an explicit skip). Null/omitted when not knowable at the call site.

model.description: The model identifier active for the session, when known. Null/omitted when not knowable at the call site.

payload.description: Event-specific detail. Permissive on purpose: emitters attach the extra fields a given eventType needs (e.g. cost, branch name, gate id) without requiring a schema-surface bump for each.
